content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted. **This is a review gate** — per our spec-driven workflow, I won't plan or write any code until you've approved it.

## 📄 Specification ready for your review

- **Feature directory**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist**: all items pass ✅

### What the spec proposes

**Three prioritized user stories** (each independently usable):

1. **P1 — Save a bookmark**: add a link by its address, with an optional title, description, and tags; invalid addresses are rejected; a title is auto-derived if none is given.
2. **P2 — Browse and find**: search by keyword (title/address/description/tags) and filter by tag, with sensible empty states.
3. **P3 — Organize and edit**: rename, re-tag, and delete bookmarks (with a delete confirmation).

**12 functional requirements**, key entities (**Bookmark**, **Tag**), and measurable success criteria (e.g. save a bookmark in under 20s, find one among 100+ in under 10s, bookmarks survive restart 100% of the time).

### Key assumptions I made (please confirm or correct)

- **Single-user** app for v1 — no accounts, login, or sharing.
- Delivered as a **web application** reviewed in a browser.
- Bookmarks stored in the **app's own local storage** — no browser-sync or external bookmark service.
- Stores **references only** — it does not fetch/archive page content or continuously check if links still work.
- **Import/export and a browser-capture extension are out of scope** for v1.

---

Please review `spec.md`. A few things worth an explicit decision:

- Are the **out-of-scope** calls right (no accounts, no import/export, no link-health checking)?
- Is anything **missing** you'd want in v1 (e.g., folders/collections in addition to tags, favorites/pinning, sorting options)?

Reply with approval or any changes. Once you approve, the next gate is **speckit-plan** (I can optionally run **speckit-clarify** first if you'd like to tighten anything).

I’m not ready to approve this version yet. Please add:

- Automatic page details when saving: title, description, favicon, and preview image, while still letting me edit the title and description.
- “Read later” status and a separate unread view.
- Reversible archiving with its own archive view, distinct from permanent deletion.
- Sorting, at least by date added and title.
- Duplicate addresses should take me to edit the existing bookmark rather than create another copy.

Tags are enough; I don’t need folders or favorites. No accounts or ongoing link-health checks is fine. I would like standard bookmark import/export in v1 so I can bring in an existing collection and take it with me later. I also expect saved notes and a preserved page snapshot, including keeping PDFs as PDFs.

## 📄 Updated specification — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

### What changed from v1

| Your request | How it's now in the spec |
|---|---|
| Auto page details (title, description, favicon, preview image), editable title/description | **US1** + FR-003, FR-004; fallback when unfetchable (FR-005) |
| Preserved page snapshot, PDFs kept as PDFs | New **US2** (P1) + FR-006–FR-008 |
| Read-later status + unread view | New **US4** + FR-014 |
| Reversible archive + archive view, distinct from delete | New **US6** + FR-016, FR-017 |
| Sort by date added and title | Folded into **US3** + FR-013 (both asc/desc) |
| Duplicate address → edit existing, not a copy | New **US7** + FR-018 (covers archived duplicates too) |
| Saved notes | New **US5** + FR-015 (also searchable) |
| Standard import/export in v1 | New **US8** + FR-020–FR-022 |

Also added: **Snapshot** and updated **Bookmark** entities, and new success criteria (SC-002 auto-fill rate, SC-004 snapshot reopen, SC-006 zero duplicates, SC-007 archive/restore, SC-008 export→re-import).

### Confirmed out of scope (per your note)
Folders, favorites, user accounts, and ongoing link-health checks.

### Two decisions baked in as assumptions — please confirm

1. **"Standard bookmark format" = the HTML bookmark file** that browsers import/export (Chrome, Firefox, Safari all speak it). On import, **nested folders map to tags** (since you don't want folders). Good, or did you have a different format in mind?
2. **Snapshots and details are captured once at save time** — no automatic re-capture. Matches your "no ongoing link-health checks."

---

Two things worth a moment before you approve:

- **Preview image vs. snapshot** are distinct: the preview image is a thumbnail shown in the list; the snapshot is the full preserved page. Both are in scope — just flagging so it's intentional.
- Anything on **snapshot scope** you'd want to pin down (e.g., is capturing a static rendering of the page enough, or do you expect interactive elements preserved)? I've left it as "content as it was at save time," which favors a faithful static capture.

Reply with approval or edits. Once approved, next gate is **speckit-plan** (or I can run **speckit-clarify** first to tighten the snapshot/import details).

Approved. The standard browser HTML bookmark format and mapping imported folders to tags both work for me. Capturing details and snapshots once at save time is also right, and a faithful static snapshot is sufficient—I don’t expect interactive elements to keep working. Both the list thumbnail and the full snapshot are intentionally in scope.

## 📐 Plan ready for review — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`

**Generated artifacts:** `plan.md`, `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`, `quickstart.md`

### Proposed technical approach

| Concern | Decision |
|---|---|
| **Shape** | Single Node.js web app — Express serves REST API (`/api/*`) + the browser UI, one `npm start` on `0.0.0.0:4000` |
| **UI** | Dependency-light vanilla JS/HTML/CSS, **no build step** (views: all / unread / archive / detail-edit) |
| **Storage** | Local **SQLite** for records; files on disk for snapshots, thumbnails, favicons — all local, durable across restarts, no external service |
| **Auto details** | Headless **Chromium (Playwright)** renders the page; parse title/description/OpenGraph image/favicon |
| **Snapshot** | Web pages → single-file **MHTML** (faithful static); **PDFs stored as original PDF bytes**; thumbnail = og:image or a screenshot |
| **Duplicates** | Normalize the URL, look up across active **and** archived; on match, open existing for editing |
| **Import/export** | Standard **Netscape bookmark HTML**; folders → tags; no duplicate addresses |
| **Testing** | `node:test` (unit/contract) + **Playwright 1.61.0** pinned to the shared browser for e2e |

**Constitution check:** the project constitution is an unpopulated template (no ratified principles), so there are no governance gates to enforce — **PASS**, no violations.

### Two choices worth your explicit nod

1. **No frontend framework** (vanilla JS, no build step). Keeps the toolchain simple and reproducible for review. If you'd prefer a React/Vue-based UI, now is the moment to say so — it changes the plan and tasks.
2. **MHTML for web-page snapshots.** It's a single self-contained file browsers render faithfully as a static page — matches your "faithful static, no interactivity" call. (PDFs are kept as PDFs regardless.)

---

Anything to adjust? Once you approve the plan, the next gate is **speckit-tasks** (the actionable, dependency-ordered breakdown), and only after that do we implement.

Approved. A simple browser interface is fine; I don’t need React or Vue. MHTML sounds suitable for the static page snapshots, with PDFs kept in their original format. Please proceed to the task breakdown.

Implementation complete. Here's the final report.

## ✅ Bookmark Manager — implementation complete

All eight approved user stories plus the polish phase are built, and **all 47 tasks in `tasks.md` are marked `[X]`**. No extension hooks were registered at any gate.

### What was built
A single Node.js/Express web app (vanilla-JS UI, no build step) serving on `0.0.0.0:4000`:

| Story | Delivered |
|---|---|
| **US1** Save + auto details | Paste a link → Chromium fetches title/description/OpenGraph image/favicon; title/description editable; invalid addresses rejected |
| **US2** Snapshot | Web pages saved as single-file **MHTML**; **PDFs preserved as PDFs**; graceful "no snapshot" fallback |
| **US3** Browse/find | Keyword search (title/address/description/notes/tags), tag filter, sort by date/title (asc/desc), empty states |
| **US4** Read-later | read/unread toggle + dedicated Unread view |
| **US5** Notes | Free-form notes, searchable |
| **US6** Archive/delete | Reversible archive + Archive view, separate permanent delete with confirmation and asset cleanup |
| **US7** Duplicates | Re-submitting a URL opens the existing bookmark for editing (incl. archived) |
| **US8** Import/export | Standard Netscape bookmark HTML; folders → tags; no duplicate addresses; counts reported |

### Verification
- **Unit + contract: 26/26 pass** (`npm test`)
- **Playwright e2e: 3/3 pass** (`npm run test:e2e`, pinned 1.61.0, shared Chromium)
- **Live boot on port 4000** confirmed; a real save fetched page details + captured snapshot; **data persisted across a restart** (SC-005)

### Two bugs found and fixed during testing (not spec/plan changes — implementation fidelity)
1. **Modal overlay blocked the whole UI**: `.overlay { display:flex }` overrode the `hidden` attribute, so the invisible dialog intercepted every click. Fixed with `[hidden]{display:none!important}` — caught by e2e.
2. **DB directory** wasn't auto-created for custom paths; `db.js` now ensures it.

### Runtime
`/work/.harness/app.json` declares `kind: application`, port 4000, `npm start`. The UI sets `data-harness-ready="true"` after the initial view loads (valid empty state included), so it's ready for you to review at **http://maker:4000**.

Artifacts remain current under `specs/001-bookmark-manager/` (spec, plan, research, data-model, contracts, quickstart, tasks). Would you like me to start the app for a review, or walk through any part?

The completed app matches the behavior we approved, and the verification report gives me enough confidence that saving, finding, organizing, preserving, importing, and exporting bookmarks all work as intended. I accept this version.
